target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full cloned-and-sorted task-registry snapshot via `listTaskRecords`. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −7 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys`
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet`
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot before loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies**
- **Gateway-proof (vi.spyOn only, zero mock):** real production `sweepCronRunSessions` exercised via a `vi.spyOn` on `listTaskRecords` to count calls. Tasks are seeded through the real `createTaskRecord` → real SQLite persistence. Sessions stored via real `session-accessor`. Only `listTaskRecords` call count is observed via spy — every other module is unmocked production code.

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/cron/_proof-reaper-gateway.test.ts --reporter verbose

 ✓ real listTaskRecords called exactly 1x per sweep (spyon, not mock)

  [REAL modules] S=50 sessions, T=20 tasks created
  listTaskRecords calls per sweep: 1
  sweep result: swept=true, pruned=42
  old path would have called listTaskRecords ~25 times (per continuation row)

 ✓ new vs old decisions: 100% match on real tasks + real reaper loop

  [correctness] old vs new: 50/50 match, 0 mismatch
  pending set size: 33

 ✓ contract: requester+owner captured, terminal excluded, non-media skipped

 ✓ S=100 sessions, real reaper: 1 listTaskRecords call (timer)

  [perf] S=100, T=200, listTaskRecords calls: 1, sweep: 34.45ms
  [perf] old path would call listTaskRecords ~50 times

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

- **`listTaskRecords` called exactly 1x per sweep** at S=50 and S=100 (old code: ~S/2 calls)
- **50/50 decisions match** between old per-row helper and new one-shot snapshot
- **Contract preserved**: requester + owner session keys both captured, terminal (succeeded) tasks excluded, chat/non-media tasks ignored
- **Real SQLite persistence**: tasks created via `createTaskRecord` go through the full production persist path (task-registry → SQLite store)
